ANA.name: Anaheim Ducks
text: The Ducks are 5-7-1 so far.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they give up dangerous chances and play fast, wide-open games.
They create chances even when shorthanded.

BOS.name: Boston Bruins
text: The Bruins are 9-4-1 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their 14 games.
Night to night, they leave most of the shooting to the forwards and sit back rather than forecheck.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but they spend a lot of time in the box.

BUF.name: Buffalo Sabres
text: The Sabres are 6-4-3 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They find a way to get their shots past the blockers and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.

CGY.name: Calgary Flames
text: The Flames are 6-7-0, still looking for their first playoff spot in four seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they fire from everywhere, though a lot of it is hopeful and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their power play has no bite.

CAR.name: Carolina Hurricanes
text: The defending champs are picking up right where they left off, 11-2-2 out of the gate, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in 13 of their 15 games.
Expect them to spend most of the night in the other team’s end and give up dangerous chances.
They create chances even when shorthanded and their penalty kill is airtight.

CHI.name: Chicago Blackhawks
text: The rebuild grinds on in Chicago: no playoffs in six seasons, and a 4-9-0 start.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They rarely block shots and spend a lot of the night in their own end.
Their power play has no bite.

COL.name: Colorado Avalanche
text: The Avalanche, playoff regulars, are 7-5-1 so far.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Night to night, they shoot from distance and play fast, wide-open games.
Their penalty kill is airtight.

CBJ.name: Columbus Blue Jackets
text: The Blue Jackets are 5-6-0, still looking for their first playoff spot in six seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and get a lot of their shots blocked.
Their penalty kill leaks.

DAL.name: Dallas Stars
text: The Stars, playoff regulars, are 7-5-1 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
On the ice, they get in front of a lot of shots and grind games down.
Their power play is lethal, but they spend a lot of time in the box.

DET.name: Detroit Red Wings
text: The Red Wings are 6-4-3, still looking for their first playoff spot in ten seasons.
They’ve played better than that record, too, winning the battle for chances more often than not.
Night to night, they get in front of a lot of shots and ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble.
They stay out of the box and their power play is lethal.

EDM.name: Edmonton Oilers
text: The Oilers are 9-2-2, which is what we’ve come to expect.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they lean hard on their top players and send their defensemen in to shoot.
Their power play is lethal, but their goaltending has let them down.

FLA.name: Florida Panthers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Panthers have bounced back to 8-4-2, winners of three straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in eight of their 14 games.
Night to night, they collapse around the net and give up the point and hound the puck in the other team’s end.
Their penalty kill is airtight and their power play is lethal.

LAK.name: Los Angeles Kings
text: The Kings have made the playoffs five years running, but they’re 4-6-2 this time.
They’ve played better than that, though, so a bit of luck could turn it around.
Expect them to settle for a lot of hopeful shots and leave most of the shooting to the forwards.

MIN.name: Minnesota Wild
text: The Wild are 9-3-3 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their 15 games.

Taking into account how much value each missing player usually adds, only the Islanders have been hit harder by absences: their regulars have missed 65 games so far, with Jared Spurgeon, Marcus Foligno and Joel Eriksson Ek still out.
Night to night, they crash the net for second chances and get pinned in their own end on long shifts.
Their goaltending has been stealing games and they stay out of the box.

MTL.name: Montréal Canadiens
text: The Canadiens are 8-3-2 so far, winners of four straight.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in nine of their 13 games.
On the ice, they get into a lot of chippy games and give up very few shots, though the ones they allow are dangerous.
They spend a lot of time in the box and their power play has no bite.

NSH.name: Nashville Predators
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Predators are 4-4-5.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Night to night, they get pinned in their own end on long shifts and crash the net for second chances.

NJD.name: New Jersey Devils
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Devils have bounced back to 9-5-0.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in twelve of their 14 games.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.

NYI.name: New York Islanders
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Islanders have bounced back to 7-4-2.
The play has been closer than the record, though.

Taking into account how much value each missing player usually adds, no team has been hit harder by absences: their regulars have missed 33 games so far, with Mathew Barzal, Matias Maccelli and Alexander Romanov still out.
Night to night, they send their defensemen in to shoot and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games, but their penalty kill leaks.

NYR.name: New York Rangers
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Rangers are 7-6-1, losers of three straight.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they get a lot of their shots blocked and get right to the net.
They spend a lot of time in the box.

OTT.name: Ottawa Senators
text: The Senators are 8-5-1 so far.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and rarely get stuck out on long shifts.
They stay out of the box, but their goaltending has let them down.

PHI.name: Philadelphia Flyers
text: The Flyers are 3-8-4 so far, losers of three straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Their game? They grind games down and get a lot of their shots blocked.

PIT.name: Pittsburgh Penguins
text: The Penguins are 5-6-2 so far.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Their game? They get right to the net and sit back rather than forecheck.

SJS.name: San Jose Sharks
text: The Sharks are 7-6-1, still looking for their first playoff spot in seven seasons.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
Their game? They ice the puck a lot to get out of trouble and hit everything that moves.
Their penalty kill leaks.

SEA.name: Seattle Kraken
text: Could this be the year? The Kraken haven’t made the playoffs in three seasons, but they’re 8-5-1 so far.
Don’t get too comfortable, though: they’ve been outchanced in most of those games, and that tends to catch up with a team.
Expect them to let the other team shoot, but mostly hopeful shots and play a finesse game.
Their penalty kill leaks and their power play has no bite.

STL.name: St. Louis Blues
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Blues are 6-6-1.
That’s about how they’ve played, too: some nights on top, some not.
Night to night, they keep things calm after the whistle and keep the other team to hopeful shots.
Their power play has no bite.

TBL.name: Tampa Bay Lightning
text: Same old Lightning: 8-3-1, and in the mix again.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in eight of their twelve games.
Expect them to get into a lot of chippy games and spend most of the night in the other team’s end.

TOR.name: Toronto Maple Leafs
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Maple Leafs are 7-6-2.
If anything the record is kind: they’ve been outchanced more often than not.
On the ice, they pounce on turnovers and find a way to get their shots past the blockers.
Their goaltending has let them down and they spend a lot of time in the box.

UTA.name: Utah Mammoth
text: The Mammoth are 9-5-0 so far.
They’ve earned it, too, with the better of the chances in twelve of their 14 games.
Their game? They rarely get stuck out on long shifts and roll all four lines.

VAN.name: Vancouver Canucks
text: Last season was one to forget in Vancouver, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 3-11-1.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Expect them to spend a lot of the night in their own end and crash the net for second chances.
Their penalty kill leaks and their goaltending has let them down.

VGK.name: Vegas Golden Knights
text: Last spring’s runners-up look hungry: they’re 9-5-1.
And it’s no mirage: they’ve had the better of the chances in eleven of their 15 games.
Expect them to keep the other team to hopeful shots and get in front of a lot of shots.
Their penalty kill is airtight and they stay out of the box.

WSH.name: Washington Capitals
text: After missing the playoffs last spring, the Capitals have bounced back to 8-4-0, winners of three straight.
The play has been closer than the record, though.
Their game? They get to the dangerous chances and get caught after turnovers too often.
Their goaltending has been stealing games.

WPG.name: Winnipeg Jets
text: Last season was one to forget in Winnipeg, and this one hasn’t started much better: they’re 4-7-3, losers of eight straight.
And honestly, they haven’t played much better than that.
Night to night, they rarely get burned after losing the puck and settle for a lot of hopeful shots.
They create chances even when shorthanded.
